structured.answer: With 750 ₪ a month for 15 years and nothing at the start, the page says I'd end up with about 179,889 ₪ in today's money, after fees and tax. It assumes 2% inflation a year and a 7% return. Its cheapest choice is an account at פסגות ניירות ערך with the fund ילין לפידות קרן מחקה S&P 500 (4D), but I'd ask my son and the bank before I signed anything.

stuck.why: It opens with English letters (S&P 500, MSCI) and a dark screen. Without the task I'd have felt it wasn't for me.
Coloured bars with many small numbers and close colours. I only took the big 'מס' figure.

findings.what: Dark background with small grey text. The lines under the big numbers and the fund details are hard to read even when enlarged.
findings.where: Whole page, especially the result cards and fund card

findings.what: The page opens with English index names and gives no plain explanation for someone used to deposits
The 7% yearly return is filled in ahead of time and never explained as a guess. The big 179,889 ₪ looks like a promise.
findings.where: תשואה בשנה box and main result

findings.what: Parts of the page moved sideways and up while I was typing in the boxes
The cost bar uses many colours that are close together, with tiny numbers inside
findings.where: 'כמה זה עולה לכם ב־15 שנים' chart

findings.what: A minus sign (−122 ₪) next to the second option is confusing and looks alarming
I only knew inflation was 2% because I pressed a button. It isn't shown next to the result.
